questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my study destination I focused on multiple factors; if there were any courses available which I was interested in, the legal system (common law), the quality of the education provided (USYD is a high ranking university in law) and my interest in the country and culture. As I have always wanted to travel Australia it seemed a natural starting point for my research, and luckily USYD had many courses available that I found very interesting, as well as a high level of education and social engagement amongst students. I especially loved that the university facilitates 200+ social clubs between students and has a very active student union that often arranges social events.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get a lot of information from the university prior to arrival and before the beginning of the semester, which makes it a lot easier to ease into studying at USYD. Highly recommend attending the introductory seminars/intro week, as a lot of useful information is given there (as well as in the emails received before the start of the semester).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of emails with useful information from my study abroad advisor from USYD, as well as an introductory seminar and the opportunity of 1:1 meetings or video calls for personal assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing situation in Australia is tough so unless you know someone who lives there, I highly recommend waiting with finding housing until you have arrived in Australia. A lot of landlords will require you to come view the property with quite short notice and have a lot of documents ready. We were very lucky and found a place through Gumtree which we signed just 2 days after viewing it, as there was a lot of other interested tenants.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure you get your landlord to help set up electricity/gas/internet if it isn't included in the price. It can be hard to find off campus housing, but if you have a bunch of friends, it is definitely worth it finding a house/big apartment etc., as it was cheaper (for us) than some student housing options. Just make sure to check the distance to the university as Sydney is huge.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once nominated by UCPH you eventually get an email from USYD with a link to their platform with the information you need to fill out. Very easy to navigate and fill out by yourself; just remember to do it before the deadline.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Study abroad advisor was available to help with any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get your courses pre-approved by UCPH ASAP after having received the list of available courses from USYD as your application must be submitted with pre-approved courses 2 weeks after you receive the enrolment email. I had to call the administration at UCPH and have them push my pre-approval application through quicker. Also aim to get 8-10 classes pre-approved even if you will only be studying four classes at USYD; that way you'll get a pre-approved class no matter whether you get your first priority or not.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses was very appropriate and at the same level as the courses at UCPH. However, as they are taught in english, certain legal terms and references to case law unknown to non-Australians makes the classes a bit harder/makes them require a bit more research.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching is very different to the one at UCPH, although classes at both universities consist of a subject being taught by the lecturer with student engagement. 

At USYD it is mandatory to attend at least 70% of classes in person in order to pass the class. Moreover, there can be/most likely is mid-semester assignments, on-call, presentations and final assignments which must be passed, which requires a lot more work throughout the semester, as they all count towards your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAWS5179: IP: Patents & Trademarks
LAWS5152: Medical Law
LAWS5163: Sports Law
LAWS5128: Media Law: Defamation and Privacy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed almost all of my courses, Media Law being the exception, but this was only due to the lecturer - the material itself was interesting and could be fairly easily understood.
Medical Law is a very interesting course but harder than the others as there is no book and the curriculum consists of PDF's (approx 1000 pages) with a collection of case law, articles and sections from various regulations. You really have to stay focused  in class in order to gather the key points and importance of the various material.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Rent doesn't cover gas/electricity/internet, so this had to be paid separately. 
You are also obligated to get an Australian insurance on top of any travel insurance you might have. This, along with the visa fees, adds up.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is expensive (as expected) so definitely try to budget more than you might end up needing. Definitely recommend batch cooking as well as groceries are not cheap (slightly more expensive than in DK).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved the fitness centre associated with USYD.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: 200+ social clubs as well as a fitness center with a special member price for USYD students. Loads of social activities throughout the semester as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like to keep active definitely sign up for the USYD gym - great facilities with a pool, tennis, squash and basketball/volleyball courts as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The Blue Mountains are a must! It's just a 2hr train ride from Sydney and has many great hikes. 
I also did a weekend trip down to Jervis Bay, a weekend trip up to Hunters Valley and longer trips to both WA (Perth-Coral Bay) and up the East Coast (Brisbane-Cairns) and I highly recommend seeing as much of Australia as you can as it is a beautiful country with many different sights to see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very close to the Danish culture, so very easy to adapt to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just make the effort and attend social events/talk to people; most people in Australia are very nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cafés close at around 14, so afternoon coffee is not an option.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity, openminded-ness and welcoming attitude of most people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join some social clubs/events/etc.
2. Most books are available online/at the library so save your money
3. Download the app "Lost on campus" as classrooms can be tricky to find

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to apply a student card before the beginning of the semester - you need it for a bunch of stuff (discounts etc.) so it just makes it easier to have it collected before all the fun begins.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to see many different parts of Australia and meeting new people along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping on top of all deadlines for assignments while still remembering to enjoy exchange and being social.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't bring sunscreen from home (it doesn't work) but definitely buy some. Also it gets a lot colder than expected so bring a jacket/hoodie.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
